transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood CSM); Sarah Patel (CISO, LumenTrust), Ravi Menon (Head of Infrastructure), Emily Cho (Security Engineer), Jamal Brooks (DevOps)
Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/pen_test_report_v1.pdf (sanitized), https://redwood.example.com/remediation_tracker.xlsx, Redwood SOC2 evidence link (partial)

Summary:
Quick review of most recent third-party pen test results run against Redwood Dedicated environment used in PoC; focus on vulnerability triage, remediation prioritization, secure SDLC/patching cadence, and follow-up retest timing. Discussed RBAC/SSO implications, KMS/encryption at rest, audit log retention, and data residency concerns. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share sanitized report and remediation tracker; LumenTrust to confirm patching windows and provide IP allowlist for VPC testing; retest scheduled in ~4 weeks pending remediation.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna run through the pen test results and remediation plan. Diego will walk through the technical findings. Sarah, Ravi, do you want to do quick intros?
[00:12] Sarah Patel: Sure, Sarah Patel, CISO at LumenTrust. We saw the initial summary you sent and have a few follow-ups about RCE-ish risk items and the patch cadence, and also curious about audit logs retention for compliance.
[00:24] Ravi Menon: Ravi here, infra. Mainly concerned about patch windows and whether redwood's dedicated nodes can be scheduled for our maintenance windows without impacting throughput.
[00:33] Diego Alvarez: Hey, Diego, Redwood SE. I'll go through the vuln list, the CVEs called out, and suggestions. Quick note: the transcript may mis-say some kernel names, so I'll repeat references as needed.
[00:44] [00:44] Diego Alvarez: Opening the findings — overall pen test flagged 18 findings: 3 critical, 5 high, 6 medium, 4 low. Critical items are around an outdated library in the operator used in the Dedicated control plane, a misconfiguration in RBAC that allowed broad cluster-admin impersonation in the test account, and a TLS cert chain issue on an internal admin endpoint.
[01:10] Sarah Patel: Can you be specific on the RBAC item, Diego? Is that in Redwood's customer-facing plane or in the private control plane for Dedicated?
[01:18] Diego Alvarez: It's in the Dedicated control plane implementation the pen tester used — basically a rolebinding that, in combination with a custom webhook, allowed escalation. We patched the code path, we already have a PR, but the concern is audit log evidence and whether you want us to rotate creds now or after your remediation window.
[01:36] Jamal Brooks: So is that a matter of us restarting pods or do you need a full deploy? Would like to avoid mid-day deploys if possible.
[01:43] Diego Alvarez: It's a code change — will require rolling deploy over a configured maintenance window. It's low time, but we recommend doing it during your low-traffic window. We can do a canary first.
[01:54] [01:54] Emily Cho: What's the exploitability on the TLS cert chain? Is it MITM risk for data in transit or limited to internal admin flows?
[02:02] Diego Alvarez: The cert issue is limited to an internal admin endpoint that is not exposed to customer traffic; still, we treat it as high because an attacker with network access to management plane could leverage it. We've rotated the cert and will push CA pinning in the next patch.
[02:18] Maya Chen: Quick pause — for compliance, Sarah, we can provide the audit log snapshots showing when the tester accessed the resource, and we can include tamper-evident hashes. Do you need that for your SOC 2 evidence?
[02:32] Sarah Patel: Yes, our auditors will want the chain of custody for the test. Also need to understand retention windows and whether logs include API caller principal and IP.
[02:41] Priya Singh: We can share log export with redaction and include IPs — redwood stores audit logs for 90 days by default, with options for longer retention in Dedicated/Private plans. That said, we'll confirm retention and the log fields available.
[02:56] [02:56] Ravi Menon: About data residency — our compliance team insists data for EU customers must remain in EU regions; was any of the test environment in a different region?
[03:06] Diego Alvarez: The testing was executed against the Dedicated environment provisioned in us-east-1 for this PoC. For full Private deployments we have region pinning and VPC-only control plane options. We can replicate the patch workflow in your EU region if you want a retest in-place.
[03:20] Sarah Patel: Good. We need the retest to be in eu-west-1 for the production rollout.
[03:26] Diego Alvarez: Noted. We'll schedule eu-west-1 retest after remediation.
[03:30] [03:30] Diego Alvarez: Now on vulnerability management — Redwood's process: immediate triage for critical/high in 72 hours, patch or mitigation within 30 days for high, 90 for medium, etc. We also run monthly vulnerability scans and quarterly third-party pen tests.
[03:46] Jamal Brooks: Do you publish SLAs for remediation timeframes as part of Dedicated contracts?
[03:51] Maya Chen: We include commitments and a remediation playbook in enterprise agreements; we'll surface that in the contract addendum if you move to Dedicated.
[03:58] [03:58] Emily Cho: For secure SDLC, do you run SCA (software composition analysis) and CI gating for high severity CVEs?
[04:06] Diego Alvarez: Yes — SCA in our CI pipeline blocks merges for critical CVEs and creates Jira issues for high ones. We also have a canary pipeline per cluster and run integration tests that exercise the management paths. Note: the pen tester found a chaining issue where a custom plugin bypassed the SCA because it was added post-approval — that's on our checklist to improve.
[04:29] Sarah Patel: That's a red flag for us — we need assurance that any third-party plugins are vetted and that there's RBAC enforcement for plugin registration.
[04:38] Diego Alvarez: Agreed, and we're adding stricter gating and audit hooks today.
[04:43] [04:43] Maya Chen: Let's walk through the top three critical findings and the mitigation status. Diego?
[04:47] Diego Alvarez: Critical 1: operator lib version x.y.z had CVE-2026-1337 — we've rolled an updated image, PR #452 merged, rolling deploy scheduled. Mitigated: yes, but we need to coordinate restart.
[05:02] Diego Alvarez: Critical 2: RBAC binding escalation — mitigation available via config change + patch; we've applied a temporary policy that removes the problematic binding in staging; prod requires deploy.
[05:14] Diego Alvarez: Critical 3: admin TLS chain — cert rotated and new chain deployed to staging; prod rotation scheduled same deploy as operator patch.
[05:24] Ravi Menon: For the rolling deploy, what's the expected downtime or degraded throughput?
[05:29] Diego Alvarez: Zero downtime expected for customer traffic — we use continuous rolling deploys with readiness probes. However, KV cache warm-up could cause small tail-latency increases for the first 5–10 minutes post-deploy. We can schedule later in the evening to minimize impact.
[05:46] [05:46] Sarah Patel: On the topic of KMS/encryption — the pen test mentions a misconfigured IAM policy that allowed read of an admin key in a test harness. Is that a problem in your production KMS integration or only in the test harness?
[05:57] Diego Alvarez: It was specific to a test harness used in the pen test setup; production KMS integrations use customer-managed keys for Dedicated/private and stricter IAM. But we'll still audit the harness and rotate keys.
[06:08] Emily Cho: Can you provide the KMS key policy and which roles have decrypt permissions? Our auditor will ask for explicit mapping.
[06:15] Diego Alvarez: Yes — we'll export the policy and map to role names. We'll sanitize any internal usernames before sharing.
[06:21] [06:21] Maya Chen: Another compliance point: SOC 2 artifacts — do you have outstanding questions on Redwood's SOC 2?
[06:28] Sarah Patel: We need the latest SOC 2 report and the scope — does it include Dedicated control plane? Also want to confirm whether audit logs are write-once and if you support log forwarding to customer SIEMs.
[06:40] Priya Singh: Latest SOC 2 Type II is shareable; scope includes Hosted and Dedicated control planes but not on-prem Private deployments by default — we can discuss scope extension. We do support log forwarding to S3/GCS or direct syslog ingestion to your SIEM with encryption in transit.
[06:56] [06:56] Jamal Brooks: Are there RBAC roles for read-only access to logs? We want to give auditors read-only access without exposing admin consoles.
[07:04] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we have granular IAM roles and can generate time-limited tokens tied to SSO.
[07:09] [07:09] Sarah Patel: On SSO — SAML/SCIM provisioning, are groups synchronized to RBAC roles automatically?
[07:16] Diego Alvarez: We support SAML for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Group mapping to RBAC is configurable; by default we map groups to roles but you can enforce allowlists.
[07:26] Sarah Patel: Good. Need that documented for our internal policy.
[07:29] [07:29] Maya Chen: Back to patch cadence — you mentioned Redwood's timelines (72h triage, 30 days for high). Can you describe the patch release train and how customers are notified?
[07:40] Diego Alvarez: We run weekly release trains for non-critical patches; critical security fixes trigger out-of-band emergency releases. Customers on Dedicated get a notification 48–72 hours before a scheduled rolling deploy and we provide detailed release notes and post-deploy validation reports.
[07:55] Ravi Menon: Can Redwood adopt our monthly first-Saturday maintenance window? We need that to align with internal change freezes.
[08:02] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated contracts can include preferred maintenance windows; we'll note that in the action items.
[08:08] [08:08] Emily Cho: For CVE tracking, is there a public tracker or do you push to a private Jira for customers?
[08:14] Diego Alvarez: We can give you a view into our vulnerability tracker for your account — not public. We'll push CVE status and mitigation timeline, and you can subscribe.
[08:23] [08:23] Sarah Patel: A couple minutess on risk acceptance — you mentioned temporary mitigations earlier. We need to document any residual risk acceptance and have an owner. Can Redwood own the mitigation until we decide?
[08:36] Maya Chen: We can operate the mitigation and own the patch execution as part of our managed Dedicated offering; we will document acceptance and track in remediation_tracker.xlsx.
[08:46] [08:46] Diego Alvarez: Quick note on testing methodology: the pen test included authenticated tests and some privileged escalation attempts. Some of the lower-severity items were false positives due to test harness behaviour; we've annotated each finding in the report.
[09:00] Jamal Brooks: How do you handle disclosure to customers if a widespread vulnerability is discovered across customers?
[09:07] Diego Alvarez: We have an incident communication playbook — if it's customer-impacting, we notify customers via email and in-console alert within 2 hours of confirmation, and we publish remediation steps and ETA.
[09:19] [09:19] Sarah Patel: Do you do CVE disclosure coordination with upstream vendors?
[09:23] Diego Alvarez: Yes. We coordinate with upstream maintainers and subscribe to major CVE feeds.
[09:29] [09:29] Maya Chen: Let's capture explicit next steps and owners — Diego will share sanitized report and tracker, Sarah will confirm patch windows, Jamal will provide IP allowlist, Redwood to schedule eu-west-1 retest in ~4 weeks.
[09:40] Sarah Patel: One more question — for audit logs we want WORM (write once read many) or some tamper-evident storage. Do you support immutability on S3 buckets for log archiving?
[09:52] Priya Singh: We support S3 Object Lock and can enable governance/compliance mode for Dedicated customers; we'll include configuration steps in the doc we share.
[10:03] Ravi Menon: On encryption keys, if we use customer-managed keys (CMK), what is the rotation cadence and who holds the key material?
[10:10] Diego Alvarez: With CMKs you control the key, and Redwood integrates with your KMS. Redwood never stores raw key material. Rotation is controlled by your KMS policy — we recommend 90 days for high-sensitivity keys but it's configurable.
[10:21] [10:21] Emily Cho: Regarding the remediation tracker, can we get a column for compliance evidence (e.g., log snapshot link)?
[10:27] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we'll add a column for evidence links and paste sanitized artifacts.
[10:31] [10:31] Maya Chen: Any blockers for proceeding with remediation as proposed?
[10:35] Sarah Patel: One ask — include explicit attestations in the report for change windows and whether any customer traffic might be affected. Otherwise good.
[10:43] Maya Chen: We'll annotate that.
[10:45] [10:45] Diego Alvarez: I'll also include a runbook for emergency rollback and verification steps.
[10:51] Jamal Brooks: For the VPC peering step, we'll need Redwood to confirm the allowed IP ranges so our firewall team can pre-authorize.
[10:58] Diego Alvarez: We'll provide the ranges; action item captured.
[11:02] [11:02] Sarah Patel: OK, let's do a quick recap of decisions and next meeting. We'll aim to confirm patch window by 2026-04-20 and Redwood will do the in-region retest in eu-west-1 the week of 2026-05-11, pending remediation.
[11:17] Maya Chen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[11:20] Priya Singh: I'll follow up with calendar invite for the retest and attach sanitized report.
[11:25] Diego Alvarez: One final note — some wording in the pen test report uses 'admin plane' and 'control plane' interchangeably; we've clarified the nomenclature in the report.
[11:34] Sarah Patel: Appreciate it. We'll review the sanitized artifacts and get back with scheduling.
[11:38] Maya Chen: Meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.

Attachments referenced:
- pen_test_report_v1.pdf (sanitized)
